expected_improvement: Exactly four elephants should become countable by arranging them as four separated full-body figures.
The elephants should read as metal by giving each elephant a shiny silver reflective surface.
The penguins should read as stone by giving each penguin gray carved rock texture.
The chase relation should become clearer by placing all four lions behind the elephants in running poses, with the elephants moving away in the same direction.
The play relation should become clearer by placing the penguins directly beside and in front of the elephants, with elephant trunks reaching toward the penguins in playful interaction.
preserve_constraints: Keep exactly four lions visible and countable.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt stated the target relations and materials but did not force a simple, verifier-readable layout. The elephant count was vulnerable because the elephants were not specified as four separated full-body instances in a row. The material attributes were described generally but not visually anchored with strong surface cues. The two relations were also too abstract: 'grouped behind' and 'interacting playfully' did not create an unmistakable chase direction or a visible play action.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Prompt under-specified the spatial layout, material visual cues, and count separation for the failed constraints.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple side-view composition with three separated groups: four lions on the left running toward four shiny metal elephants in the center, and five gray stone penguins on the right/front of the elephants. Make all animals full-body, separated, and countable. Use strong material cues on the target objects only: reflective silver metal elephants and carved gray stone penguins. Make relations explicit with directional running poses for the chase and elephant trunks reaching toward the penguins for playful interaction.
regression_risks: The generator may add extra animals while trying to fill the scene.
The generator may merge elephants together, causing the elephant count to fail again.
The generator may make penguins normal black-and-white instead of stone.
The generator may make elephants normal gray skin instead of metal.
The generator may focus on play and weaken the lions-chasing-elephants relation.
repair_constraints: Show exactly four elephants, each as a separate full-body elephant with visible gaps between them; no extra elephants and no merged elephant bodies.
Make every elephant visibly made of shiny silver metal, with reflective metallic surfaces; do not make the lions or penguins metal.
Place the four lions behind the elephants, running toward the elephants, while the elephants face and move away from the lions, so the lions are clearly chasing the elephants.

Make the four metal elephants visibly playing with the five penguins by positioning the penguins directly near the elephants and showing the elephants reaching their trunks toward the penguins in a playful interaction.
Make every penguin visibly made of gray stone, with carved rock texture; do not make the lions or elephants stone.
